summary: 1. Two new meeting notes landed, both 1-Sep: a daily standup and an internal justification meeting held ahead of Maaden's formal response to August's underperformance. 2. Maaden issued a formal notice of unsatisfactory August production, Ivan Anthony requested a written justification (what happened, what changes going forward), and Maaden is bringing in external "Outliners" consultants to assess the operation. 3. New Wiki article [[august-2026-performance-review-escalation]] synthesises the root causes named (workforce rotation, a self-described truck-allocation strategy error, tire-workshop understaffing, engine/final-drive failure, no water/dust suppressant), the structural planning disputes (top-down annual target, no September plan issued eight days into the fiscal month equivalent, a 2027 365-day-calendar request), the geological block-model-vs-drilled-grade mismatch, an unannounced crusher speed increase, and a capex gap ($8M received vs $39M requested, against Mansoura's reported $40M). 2. 4. A parallel Maaden-side thread (Week 35 planning review, Katongo Kangwa) quantifies the same underlying shortfall at 296.2 kt against the 7+5 forecast — the same figure [[kaizen-load-haul-efficiency]] already tracks as Peter's recovery-plan target, confirming both threads point at one number. 3. 5. Survey reconciliation Day 7 (file dated 1-Sep, reconciling Aug 31 production): trucks 16,306 BCM vs survey 15,067 BCM, gap narrows to -8.22% — the second straight day of improvement after Day 6's outright client rejection — though no reply to that rejection has surfaced yet. 6. MTD gap through Day 7: -7,153 BCM (-5.45%). 4. 7. The Distance report workbook's Aug 31 tab is populated with real per-block haul data for the first time, breaking a standing blank-template pattern this KB has tracked for weeks. 5. 8. Safety: LV105 skipped its mandatory morning brake test (Peter Anthony asked directly for driver statements); a new directive requires trucks to park and stop entirely — not just drive cautiously — under unsafe night dust/visibility conditions; Stage 6 is down to one working excavator because overspill has crowded out the second, with a real risk of running most of the week on one dig face if a backup area isn't ready in time. 9. Five already ingested at prior passes. One is an empty template stub ("Meeting @Today," both structured-summary and transcript blocks blank) — skipped, not a real meeting note. Two genuinely new, both created 1-Sep: "Mining Operations Daily Review Meeting" and "Mining Operations August Performance Review & Justification Meeting" — both written verbatim to RAW. Found one new survey file (Day 7), three production workbooks re-touched after that write time (Distance report, Equipment running hours, Grade Control — only Distance report carried genuinely new content), and five files the 101st pass had explicitly flagged as out of scope for its dashboard-only run: one in `Safety Report/` (LV105 brake-test email) and four in `Maaden Plans/Mitigation Plan/` (the HOD meeting call, the original Maaden underperformance memo and Ivan's forward, and the Week 35 planning review thread).
